compute.reported_as: Supplemental Material Sec. I.B: To further reduce the computational cost, we impose full translational invariance on the f_ij parameters by considering a f_ij sublattice. When this sublattice contains M spins, the number of independent variational parameters f_ij is reduced to M × Ns ∼ O(Ns), whereas without assuming translational symmetry, the number of f_ij is (Ns × Ns) ∼ O(Ns^2). ... We therefore take M = 16 in simulations of the 3D pyrochlore lattice, while M = 2 × 2 × 16 = 64 for simulations of the quasi-2D super-tetrahedron square lattice (STSL). ... Sec. I.E: These parameters are optimized by the natural gradient (or equivalently stochastic reconfiguration) method [12-14] with the help of the conjugate gradient method [12, 15]. This allows us to access system sizes as large as Ns = 1024 sites by reducing memory and computational cost [2]. ... Sec. I.G: In principle, higher-power Lanczos steps are possible and will improve the energy even further, however are very costly, which is the reason why we consider only the first-step Lanczos method in this work. ... SM Sec. V: Linear extrapolation to zero variance has been done for 20 to 40 statistically independent measurements of the energy-eigenvalues from a singly optimized wave function within mVMC and mVMC-RBM, in combination with the first Lanczos step. ... Acknowledgments: This work was supported by MEXT as "Program for Promoting Researches on the Supercomputer Fugaku" ... and used computational resources of supercomputer Fugaku provided by the RIKEN Center for Computational Science (Project ID: hp200132, No. hp210163, and No. hp220166). Part of the computation was done using the HPC facilities provided by the Supercomputer Center of the Institute for Solid State Physics, the University of Tokyo, and computational resources of the supercomputer Fugaku provided by R-CCS through the HPCI System Research Project (Project ID: hp230169 and hp120281).
compute.source: Supplemental Material Secs. I.B, I.E, I.G, V (Tables SI-SIII); main-text Acknowledgments, arXiv:2311.11561 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: No parameter count stated for this mVMC-RBM/Lanczos wave function: the pair-product part has M × Ns = 16 × 128 = 2048 f_ij parameters by the stated formula, but the RBM size (number of hidden units) is not given anywhere in the paper or Supplement (the '128 RBM neurons' in the method label comes from VarBench's metadata/script, not from the paper text). No sample count for the energy evaluation, no iteration count, no wall-clock, core or node count; only Fugaku and ISSP supercomputers are named. Fig. 6 caption (STSL correlations) mentions 5-10 independent bins of more than 10^4 Monte Carlo steps, which is for correlation functions of a different model.

compute.reported_as: Introduction: Exploiting the SU(2) symmetry of the model [50-53], we keep up to 20000 SU(2) states, (typically equivalent to ≳ 80000 U(1) states). ... Method: For small bond dimensions (χ ≲ 2000) we use the two-site version of the DMRG, and switch to the one-site variant to optimize the wave function for larger χ. ... we use the reliable two-site variance estimation to extrapolate towards the error-free case [56], because calculation of the full variance would be impractical due to its cost. It turns out that even the calculation of the two-site variance becomes too costly for clusters with more than ∼ 100 sites and bond dimensions ≳ 8000. In certain cases, we revert to the usage of the two-site DMRG and extrapolate as a function of the truncation error (cf. 108-site cluster). ... Fig. 5 caption: The corresponding maximal bond dimensions for the 32, 64, 108 and 128-site clusters are 20000, 16000, 16000 and 12000 respectively. ... Given the scaling of the computational effort with system size, the study of much larger clusters with the present method is, however, out of reach. ... Acknowledgments: Some of the data presented here was produced using the SyTen toolkit, originally created by Claudius Hubig.
compute.source: Introduction (max SU(2) states); Methods paragraphs; Fig. 5 caption (maximal bond dimension per cluster); Acknowledgments, arXiv:2010.03563 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: bond_dimension = maximal SU(2) bond dimension stated for the 128-site cluster (Fig. 5 caption; the paper-wide maximum is 20000 SU(2) states ≈ ≳80000 U(1) states); the row energy is the χ→∞ extrapolation (linear in the two-site variance) of the finite-χ series up to that value. No wall-clock, core count, memory or hours stated anywhere (main text, Figs. 1-8 captions, Tables I-IV, Appendices A-D); only the qualitative remarks quoted. Code: SyTen.
